$comment: Pack Rat bridge protocol v1. Draft-07 style, restricted to the keyword subset app/schema/validate.mts supports (no $ref/oneOf), so this file holds three independent schemas — command, result and status — each validated separately (app/contracts.test.mts does one validate() call per shape). command = one line of <dataDir>/bridge/<adapter-id>/queue.jsonl (app/config.mts's paths.bridgeQueueFor(adapter) — per adapter, not a fixed 'tazuo'), written by POST /api/bridge (app/vault-server.mts, resolving <adapter-id> from settings.client.adapter) and read by that adapter's own packrat-bridge.py (e.g. adapters/tazuo/packrat-bridge.py). result = one entry of status.results, keyed by the command's id. status = <dataDir>/bridge/<adapter-id>/status.json (paths.bridgeStatusFor(adapter)), written by that adapter's packrat-bridge.py (alive is always rfc3339_now(); a clean stop adds stopped:true, never the old numeric 0) and read only through app/bridge-status.mts's readBridgeStatus (GET /api/bridge/status and the Organize service). Every queue line carries protocol: a bridge refuses a line in a newer protocol than it reads.

protocol.$comment: The protocol this line is written in: app/bridge-contract.mts's BRIDGE_PROTOCOL. Every packrat-bridge.py refuses a line in a newer protocol than its own PROTOCOL (its capabilities.json's protocol) and reads a line with none, from an app older than the field, as protocol 1.

id.$comment: The app writes a 36-character randomUUID(). 64 matches MAX_ID in every packrat-bridge.py, which refuses a longer id: results are keyed by id, so an unbounded one would grow status.json.

name.$comment: Only ever printed on screen. 120 matches MAX_NAME in every packrat-bridge.py, which truncates to it. POST /api/bridge validates every queue line against this schema (app/schema/validate.mts implements maxLength), so an over-long name is refused at the route with a 400 as well as truncated by the adapters.

chain.$comment: The container chain the bridge opens, outermost first. Capped at 8 — app/ui/bridge.mts's chainOf() walks at most 8 parents, and the scanner's own MAX_NEST is 4, so nothing legitimate is longer. Enforced twice: POST /api/bridge validates every queue line against this schema (app/schema/validate.mts implements maxItems) and refuses a longer chain with a 400, and each adapter's packrat-bridge.py re-checks it (MAX_CHAIN).

pos.$comment: The root container's world tile, or null when the app has none on file. x/y bounds are the widest UO facet (Britannia, 7168x4096); every other facet is smaller, so this is a sanity bound rather than a per-facet one. Each adapter's packrat-bridge.py re-validates this exact shape itself and additionally refuses a destination further than MAX_WALK_TILES (24 tiles, the client's own view range) from where the character is standing — a queue line must never be able to walk a character across the map.

facet.$comment: 0 Felucca, 1 Trammel, 2 Ilshenar, 3 Malas, 4 Tokuno, 5 Ter Mur. Optional. The scanners record it on a ground root's pos (scan schema, containers.pos.facet), the fold keeps it, and POST /api/bridge forwards the root's pos with it; the bridges validate it but do not act on it yet.

queuedAt.$comment: RFC 3339, same pattern as result.t — POST /api/bridge writes new Date().toISOString(). Each bridge parses it and refuses a command older than 60 s (a replayed backlog) or more than 5 s in the future.

partial.$comment: A trip only: the backpack or the character's carry weight ended the take phase early.

stopped.$comment: A trip only: the stop flag (POST /api/bridge/stop) or the Script Manager's Stop ended it between steps.

ms.$comment: A trip only, optional: how long the whole trip took, in milliseconds (TazUO 2.9.0 onward).

steps.$comment: A trip only (bridge-trip.v1.schema.json): one entry per step carried out or skipped, in execution order.

ms.$comment: Optional: how long the step took (walk, opening and move), in milliseconds; 0 for a skipped step.

status.$comment: Open, so a newer bridge's added field never makes this app read the bridge as offline. app/bridge-status.mts's readBridgeStatus is the one reader, and it checks every status against this schema.

alive.$comment: RFC 3339. A number is the epoch seconds an older bridge build wrote, still read.

adapter.$comment: The running bridge itself (TazUO 2.16.0, Razor Enhanced 1.12.0 and later): its adapter id, script version, the newest queue-line protocol it reads, and every action and feature it has. Left out by older bridges, which the app then judges by the newest scan and the shipped manifest. readBridgeStatus checks it on its own: a block off this shape is dropped, as if an older bridge had written the status, and the rest of the status still reads.
